## Early life and education
> Just to be clear, I didn't go to film school because I couldn't get into film school. My father knew I wanted to be a filmmaker, but he advised me to get what he referred to as 'a real degree in a real subject,' so I'd have something to fall back on and then you can go to film school afterwards, which turned out not to be the case. So I studied English because that was the academic subject that I was best at and inclined most towards. But what I found when I studied at English at UCL, is it greatly informed my filmmaking process, my writing process. I started to become more at ease with a lot of the literary concepts that underlie film criticism in particular.
— Nolan on his education[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-usatodaycannes-4)
Christopher Edward Nolan was born on 30 July 1970 in the [Westminster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westminster "Westminster") district of London.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-5)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-biography_20240310-6) His father, Brendan James Nolan (1936[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-7)–2009),[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-Shone2014-8) was a British advertising executive of Irish descent[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-9) who worked as a creative director. His mother, Christina Jensen (born 1942),[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-10) is an American former flight attendant from [Evanston, Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evanston,_Illinois "Evanston, Illinois"); she also worked as a teacher of English. He has an older brother, Matthew, and a younger brother, [Jonathan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Nolan "Jonathan Nolan"), also a filmmaker. The three brothers were raised [Catholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic "Catholic") in [Highgate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highgate "Highgate") and spent their summers in Evanston.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-ft_20230721-11)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-YouTube_PqGrR2Upz0M-12) Nolan also spent time living in Chicago during his youth, and he holds dual British and American citizenship.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christophe

## History
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Slade_School_of_Fine_Art&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9b/SLADE_1905_B_sampled.jpeg/250px-SLADE_1905_B_sampled.jpeg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:SLADE_1905_B_sampled.jpeg)Students at the Slade in 1905
The school was founded in University College on 2 October 1871 following an endowment from the will of the lawyer and philanthropist [Felix Slade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Felix_Slade "Felix Slade") (1788–1868) who bequeathed £35,000 to establish three Chairs in [Fine Art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fine_Art "Fine Art"), to be based at Oxford University, Cambridge University and [University College London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_College_London "University College London"). An additional six scholarships of £50 per annum were endowed to University College. The college itself provided £5000 to build the Slade School as part of the college quadrangle in Gower Street, premises which the School still occupies today.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slade_School_of_Fine_Art#cite_note-5)
Distinguished past teachers include [Henry Tonks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Tonks "Henry Tonks"), [Wilson Steer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilson_Steer "Wilson Steer"), [Randolph Schwabe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randolph_Schwabe "Randolph Schwabe"), [William Coldstream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Coldstream "William Coldstream"), [Andrew Forge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Forge "Andrew Forge"), [Lucian Freud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucian_Freud "Lucian Freud"), [John Hilliard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hilliard_\(artist\) "John Hilliard \(artist\)"), [Bruce McLean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_McLean "Bruce McLean"), [Alfred Gerrard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Gerrard "Alfred Gerrard") and [Phyllida Barlow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phyllida_Barlow "Phyllida Barlow"). [Edward Allington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Allington "Edward Allington") was Professor of Fine Art and Head of Graduate Sculpture until his death in 2017.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slade_School_of_Fine_Art#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slade_School_of_Fine_Art#cite_
